newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall in profit-taking.

text.p: Shares on the Jordan stock exchange slipped again on Wednesday in quiet trade after a bout of profit taking, brokers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.42 percent to 153.24 points in business worth 797,000 dinars ($1.12 million), just a quarter of Tuesday's turnover.

Brokers said underlying sentiment remained strong, boosted by the prospect of greater trade with Baghdad as Iraqi oil once more flowed to world markets. But uncertainty persisted over how much Jordanian businesses stood to benefit.
"The Iraqi issue is not too clear, but it is positive," said Samir Jaradat, an investment banker with Jordan Investment Finance Bank.

Services firm Unified Company rose strongly to two dinars in trade worth 100,000 dinars. Arab Pharmaceutical Chemicals and Arab Pharmarceutical Manufacturers were also in demand and rose to 1.57 dinars and 3.66 dinars.

Jaradat said brokers expected Jordanian transport firms to benefit first from the expected flow of food and medicine into Iraq. "Medical companies will be second to feel it, and industry will be third."
"We're going to be competing openly for business now, so quality is going to be an issue for industry," he added.
Uncertainty over the terms of Jordan's 1997 trade protocol with Iraq, under which Iraq supplies Jordan with cheap oil in return for goods exempted from U.N. sanctions, also reined in market optimism.
Jaradat said he expected active trade on the market for the remaining weeks of 1996, with sentiment particularly sensitive to scraps of news about business with Baghdad.
Shares in 18 companies rose on Wednesday but they were outnumbered by profit-taking in 25 falling shares. Another 16 shares were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of 45 best-traded shares rose 0.23 percent 82.84 points, still 13.27 percent down on last year.
